title: O, Could We Speak the Matchless Worth
description: O, Could We Speak the Matchless Worth in Tonic Solfa to MERIBAH, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Samuel Medley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 240 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Excellency of Christ”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MERIBAH; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, could we speak the match-less worth, O, could we sound the glo-ries forth, Which in our Sa-viour shine, We'd soar, and touch the heav-enly strings, And vie with Ga-briel, while he sings, In notes al-most di-vine.

lines: O, could we speak the matchless worth,
O, could we sound the glories forth,
We'd soar, and touch the heavenly strings,
And vie with Gabriel, while he sings,
We'd sing the characters he bears,
And all the forms of love he wears,
In loftiest songs of sweetest praise,
O, the delightful day will come,
When Christ our Lord will bring us home
And we shall see his face;
Then, with our Saviour, Brother, Friend,

licence: Public domain: Samuel Medley died in 1799.
credits: Words by Samuel Medley (1738–1799), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MERIBAH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
